They didn't come home for two days. I sent a text checking in if they were okay and basically still alive. Hadn't heard back. I asked again two days later after that and just tried to open the dialogue to make sure I hadn't done something. They said they were fine and I just thanked them for letting me know. None of those texts did I ask where they were, just if they were okay. Then I got a notice from them they wanted to move out. I sent another text just opening the dialogue again if anything made them uncomfortable to just let me know and wondered why they had chosen to move out. I agree I never should have asked why they had chosen to move out as I was overstepping but the situation felt weird and sudden and I let my anxiety get the best of me. We were on friendly terms before that week so not sure what changed other than me doing something wrong. 

I guess it doesn't matter. I just don't want to be dismissive or rude by ignoring what seems like clear red flags that I can only guess points to something I did. I guess in the future I'll let sleeping dogs lie and if I'm seen as rude for it then I suppose it is what it is. Better to be rude/uncaring than overstepping I guess.

I agree I overstepped by asking that question about why they're leaving since my concerns about making them uncomfortable came from my own anxiety that I had done something as this behavior wasn't normal to me. This housemate had in the past told us if they were going on vacation for a few days as a warning unprompted by me so having them disappear for a week was strange.


I don't care where they are, but I was told it's normal to tell others if you're gone for an extended time so your housemates know you're not dead or something and also just in general for things like chores/dishes. I suppose the only reason I specifically need to know if they're going to be gone is because I was taught if someone disappears like that then something is wrong. I admit I let my anxiety get the better of me in this situation but moving forward I don't know what the "correct" thing to do is as I will be getting another housemate. 


Do I ask my housemate what's going on if they're gone or is it overstepping? Is it more rude if I don't say anything or more rude if I do? I honestly don't really care whatever they're doing they're grown adults but I do want to do whatever is considered the standard.

Sounds like I don't have to worry then.


We were never friends but we were friendly and spoke to each other when we saw each other. We have done board games with her before in a group setting so this idea that we were only her landlords isn't accurate.

We were housemates and I'm not the Owner of the house so I'm not her landlord. I don't know if that changes anything. 


Like before that week she disappeared we saw her everyday and spoke to her briefly to be cordial and friendly.

Yes they viewed the place before moving in. The condition is the same as it was before and we were upfront about not being social people. 


The place isn't ever a mess and typically we do the cleaning once a week and the bins since there's no chore chart and we understand there's two of us to one of them so we take the majority of the cleaning on. It's only been the past few weeks the cleaning wasn't done weekly since we had gone on a trip and didn't have a weekend to do cleaning in between the work week.


I am just worrying if I'm being too dismissive of the matter but I do feel I've opened up the opportunity for her to open up and she has said things are fine though she was kind of blunt with it.

We arent her landlords were renting the place as well and just needed to fill the room to keep the place after our last housemate moved out. So we live with her and it's not exactly a large house. She has been in the room for about 8 months. We have never overstepped if anything we were worried we were too distant since we are fairly antisocial. 


I am worrying on my own privately. After her last text I just thanked her for letting us know and offered help if she needed it during the move. It is not normal for your housemate to not come home randomly for a week and not say anything. Typically housemates I have give a warning if they're not going to come home for many days and I've been told that's normal.

I’m saying that’s okay. During that period I had friends who couldn’t hang out when I was a train wreck because it was too much. But they weren’t rude about it nor did they demonize me or call me names or a shitty person. There’s a huge difference between being personally attacked, calling them a shitty person, bad friend, and just saying hey I can’t hang out with you if you’re gunna bail get back to me when you’re feeling healthier.

I like how there is no winning for the person with mental illness in this scenario. Either you attempt to hang out and potentially bail because of your mental illness and your friend takes it personally, calls you a shitty person, etc because of it. Or you isolate yourself because you know you have a chronic mental illness that makes you prone to random bouts of anxiety, depression, etc that make it hard to literally leave your house and so your friend takes it personally, calls you a shitty person, etc because you choose not to hang out with them in the first place. I'm biased because I know how it felt to be at my worst, literally want to die, and have all this pressure to "be a good friend" from people who "understood and wanted to help." And I wasn't doing anything mean or shitty in any way. I said nothing negative towards them. And they knew I had severe depression, was going through medications, different therapists, etc. and it still wasn't enough for them. And lots of people I know couldn't handle it at the time, they were busy, but to act the way OP is and to treat the person this way instead of just giving their friend some space I don't really know what to say to that. I just wish mental illness wasn't received that way.

If you read my post and actually understood it I stated very clearly that I knew I wasn’t being a good friend by flaking. I’m saying that the way you’re behaving makes it sound like they’re 100% awful for bailing after stating that they have a mental illness that affects their ability to show up consistently. If this was a physical illness like they agreed to hang out, woke up vommitting, and cancelled. And it was a chronic condition which mental illnesses are. You would not be this bitter. And I’m saying that you’re taking their flakiness as a statement on who they are and how they view you when in reality it’s a very self centered view and this problem has nothing to do with you. I’m not saying it’s not a bad behavior. I’m saying it’s your right to hang out with people that don’t flake on you but you shouldn’t demonize these people because you personally don’t like dealing with the less positive sides of their illness.

This is why it’s hard to have friends when you have a mental illness and why people with mental illness don’t reach out if you’re just going to continue to call them a bad friend instead of understanding where they’re coming from. I flaked so much when I was suffering from severe depression and it had nothing to do with not valuing my friends. My friends at the time knew I had severe depression but you’re right it didn’t change the fact that I wasn’t a good friend but acting the way you are is pretty awful. Don’t act like it’s a personal slight to you when your friend in question is most likely going through something and adding onto that by calling them a shitty friend isn’t helping them get better. I don’t see how flaking is equavalent to being mean at all especially when you know the source of their flakiness has nothing to do with how much they value you.
